title: Proverbs Bible Quiz - Chapter 25
description: Ten questions on Proverbs 25: proverbs copied by Hezekiah's men, fitly spoken words, and kindness to an enemy.

questions.text: Who copied out these proverbs of Solomon, according to the first verse?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:1 says these also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

answers.text: The scribes of David the king
The elders of the land of Israel
The men of Hezekiah king of Judah
The sons of Solomon the king

questions.text: What is the glory of God, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:2 says it is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.

answers.text: To conceal a thing
To search out a matter
To judge the nations
To dwell in thick darkness

questions.text: Why should you not exalt yourself in the presence of the king?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:6-7 says it is better that it be said to you, "Come up here," than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince.

answers.text: For the king sees every heart of man
For pride goes before a sudden fall
For the great men there will mock you
For it is better to be told "Come up here"

questions.text: What is a word fitly spoken compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:11 says a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.

answers.text: A honeycomb, sweet to the soul
Apples of gold in settings of silver
An ornament of fine gold
Cold water to a thirsty soul

questions.text: What is a faithful messenger like to those who send him?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:13 says as the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him, for he refreshes the soul of his masters.

answers.text: The cold of snow in the time of harvest
Dew on the grass
A cloud of the spring rain
Good news from a far country

questions.text: What does a soft tongue break, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:15 says by patience a ruler is persuaded, and a soft tongue breaks the bone.

answers.text: The heart
The sword
The dam
The bone

questions.text: Why should your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:17 says let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.

answers.text: Lest you learn his ways
Lest he be weary of you, and hate you
Lest you covet his goods
Lest his wife deceive you

questions.text: What should you give your enemy if he is hungry, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:21 says if your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

answers.text: A place at your table
Half of your harvest
Food to eat
Silver and gold

questions.text: What is good news from a far country compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:25 says like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.

answers.text: Honey from the comb
The light of the morning
Rain in harvest
Cold water to a thirsty soul

questions.text: What is a man whose spirit is without restraint compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 25:28 says like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.

answers.text: A city broken down and without walls
A muddied spring and polluted well
A ship tossed without a rudder
A house built upon the sand
